sections.overview: Pipistrellus raceyi is a small vesper bat known from Madagascar.
sections.identification: Its description separates it from related pipistrelles by skull, teeth, wings and male anatomy.
sections.habitat: Records come from lowland eastern and western sites, including farmland and dry forest.
sections.diet: The original account gives no direct prey observations.
sections.behavior: At one eastern site, bats used a hollow in an occupied building wall as a day roost.
sections.reproduction: Reproductive observations were limited in the original study.
sections.ecology: Known records span human-modified eastern sites and dry western habitats.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database currently lists it as Not Evaluated; older papers used Data Deficient.

sources.title: A description of a new species of Pipistrellus from Madagascar — Acta Chiropterologica
